linear.name: linear systems ẋ = A x
linear.summary: the canonical 2×2 linear systems classified by trace and determinant, sharing one plane (pick a system's F for streamlines / glyphs, its |F| or invariant for colour): saddle, stable / unstable node, stable / unstable spiral, center, star, improper node, a line of equilibria

gradient.name: gradient flow ẋ = −∇V
gradient.summary: steepest descent on a double-double well: 4 stable nodes, 4 saddles, 1 source, the potential's isolines orthogonal to the flow

pendulum.name: damped pendulum
pendulum.summary: θ̈ = −sin θ − γ θ̇: the energy H (isolines = frictionless orbits, separatrix at H = 2), its dissipation Ḣ ≤ 0, a captured rotating orbit

duffing.name: Duffing double well
duffing.summary: ẍ = x − x³ − δ ẋ: two attracting wells and the saddle between them; the undamped separatrix is the figure-eight H = 0

vanderpol.name: Van der Pol oscillator
vanderpol.summary: a relaxation oscillator: an unstable spiral inside a globally attracting limit cycle (drawn, integrated to convergence)

hopf.name: Hopf normal form
hopf.summary: the supercritical Hopf normal form after the bifurcation: repelling origin, circular limit cycle of radius √μ, the radial rate d(r²)/dt as the trapping mechanism

lotka.name: Lotka–Volterra predator–prey
lotka.summary: predator–prey: a nonlinear center at coexistence, a saddle at extinction, the conserved C whose isolines are the cycles

competition.name: competing species (rabbits vs sheep)
competition.summary: bistable competition: two stable nodes, a saddle, the separatrix between the basins (the saddle's stable manifold, integrated backwards)

saddlefocus.name: saddle-focus (3D linear)
saddlefocus.summary: the 3D linear saddle-focus: a stable spiral plane and an unstable axis

gradient3.name: gradient flow ẋ = −∇V (3D)
gradient3.summary: steepest descent on a triple double well: 8 sinks, 18 saddles of index 1 and 2, 1 source, isosurfaces of V normal to the flow

lorenz.name: Lorenz system
lorenz.summary: σ = 10, ρ = 28, β = 8/3: three saddle-type equilibria, a strange attractor (30 time units drawn), a trapping ellipsoid and its Lyapunov derivative

rossler.name: Rössler system
rossler.summary: a = b = 0.2, c = 5.7: the spiral-and-fold strange attractor (150 time units drawn), the divergence marking the fold

linear/saddle/F.name: saddle/F
linear/saddle/F.details: ẋ = y, ẏ = x: eigenvalues ±1 along the diagonals (1, 1) (unstable) and (1, −1) (stable). x² − y² is conserved: the orbits are hyperbolas, the diagonals the separatrices.

linear/saddle/inv.name: saddle/x² − y²
linear/saddle/inv.details: The saddle's first integral: hyperbolic orbits, the asymptotes are the stable and unstable manifolds.

linear/node-/F.name: stable node/F
linear/node-/F.details: A = [[−2, 1], [1, −2]]: eigenvalues −1 (slow, along (1, 1)) and −3 (fast, along (1, −1)). Every orbit approaches the origin tangent to the slow eigendirection.

linear/node-/lyap.name: stable node/|x|²/2
linear/node-/lyap.details: A quadratic Lyapunov function: A is symmetric negative definite, so |x|² decreases along every orbit.

linear/node+/F.name: unstable node/F
linear/node+/F.details: The stable node with time reversed: eigenvalues +1 and +3; every orbit leaves the origin (a source).
linear/node+/F.summary: The stable node with time reversed

linear/spiral-/F.name: stable spiral/F
linear/spiral-/F.details: ẋ = −0.3x − y, ẏ = x − 0.3y: eigenvalues −0.3 ± i; orbits spiral counter-clockwise into the origin (a stable focus).

linear/spiral+/F.name: unstable spiral/F
linear/spiral+/F.details: Eigenvalues 0.3 ± i: orbits spiral outward (an unstable focus, a repellor).

linear/center/F.name: center/F
linear/center/F.details: ẋ = −y, ẏ = x: eigenvalues ±i; the harmonic oscillator. Every orbit is a circle, H = |x|²/2 is conserved. Not structurally stable: any damping turns it into a spiral.

linear/center/H.name: center/H = |x|²/2
linear/center/H.details: The conserved energy; its isolines ARE the orbits.
linear/center/H.summary: The conserved energy; its isolines ARE the orbits

linear/star/F.name: star node/F
linear/star/F.details: A = −I: a double eigenvalue −1 with two independent eigenvectors; orbits are straight rays into the origin.

linear/improper/F.name: improper node/F
linear/improper/F.details: A Jordan block, double eigenvalue −1 with a single eigenvector (1, 0): every orbit arrives tangent to the x axis, sheared around.
linear/improper/F.summary: A Jordan block, double eigenvalue −1 with a single eigenvector (1, 0)

linear/line/F.name: equilibrium line/F
linear/line/F.details: ẋ = −x, ẏ = 0: det A = 0; every point of the y axis is an equilibrium (non-isolated), reached along horizontal lines.

gradient/F.name: F
gradient/F.details: F = −∇V = (x − x³, y − y³): the steepest-descent flow of the double-double well V. Streamlines cross the isolines of V at right angles.

gradient/V.name: V
gradient/V.details: V = ¼(x² − 1)² + ¼(y² − 1)²: four minima (±1, ±1), four saddles (±1, 0), (0, ±1), one maximum (0, 0). A Morse function; the flow's equilibria are its critical points, their index the number of unstable directions.

gradient/speed.name: |F|
gradient/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
gradient/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

gradient/gradV.name: ∇V
gradient/gradV.summary: the exact gradient of the potential; F = −∇V

gradient/div.name: ∇·F
gradient/div.details: ∇·F = −ΔV = 2 − 3x² − 3y²: the flow expands area near the maximum and contracts it near the minima.

pendulum/F.name: F
pendulum/F.summary: ẋ = y, ẏ = −sin x − γ y (γ = 0.25)
pendulum/F.details: ẋ = y, ẏ = −sin x − γ y (γ = 0.25): angle x, angular velocity y. Stable spirals at x = 2kπ, saddles at x = (2k+1)π; the damping makes the separatrices of the frictionless pendulum spiral into the wells.

pendulum/H.name: H
pendulum/H.details: H = y²/2 + 1 − cos x, the energy of the frictionless pendulum. Its isolines are the undamped orbits: libration below H = 2, the separatrix at H = 2 (the homoclinic orbits of the saddles), rotation above.
pendulum/H.summary: H = y²/2 + 1 − cos x, the energy of the frictionless pendulum

pendulum/speed.name: |F|
pendulum/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
pendulum/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

pendulum/F0.name: F₀ (undamped)
pendulum/F0.details: The frictionless pendulum ẋ = y, ẏ = −sin x: a Hamiltonian flow, H is conserved, the equilibria at x = 2kπ are centers.
pendulum/F0.summary: The frictionless pendulum ẋ = y, ẏ = −sin x

pendulum/Hdot.name: ∇H·F
pendulum/Hdot.details: Ḣ = ∇H·F = −γ y²: the energy dissipated by the damping, zero only on the x axis (LaSalle: orbits still converge to the wells).

duffing/F.name: F
duffing/F.summary: ẋ = y, ẏ = x − x³ − δ y (δ = 0.25)
duffing/F.details: ẋ = y, ẏ = x − x³ − δ y (δ = 0.25): a particle in the double well V = x⁴/4 − x²/2 with friction. Stable spirals at (±1, 0), a saddle at the origin whose stable manifold separates the two basins.

duffing/H.name: H
duffing/H.details: H = y²/2 + x⁴/4 − x²/2: the energy. The figure-eight isoline H = 0 is the separatrix of the undamped system (two homoclinic loops of the saddle).

duffing/speed.name: |F|
duffing/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
duffing/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

duffing/V.name: V(x)
duffing/V.details: The double-well potential x⁴/4 − x²/2 (independent of y).
duffing/V.summary: The double-well potential x⁴/4 − x²/2 (independent of y)

duffing/F0.name: F₀ (undamped)
duffing/F0.details: ẋ = y, ẏ = x − x³: Hamiltonian, H conserved; centers at (±1, 0), the saddle's homoclinic figure-eight at H = 0.

vanderpol/F.name: F
vanderpol/F.summary: ẋ = y, ẏ = μ(1 − x²) y − x (μ = 1)
vanderpol/F.details: ẋ = y, ẏ = μ(1 − x²) y − x (μ = 1): negative damping for |x| < 1, positive outside. The origin is an unstable spiral; every other orbit winds onto the unique limit cycle (Liénard's theorem).

vanderpol/speed.name: |F|
vanderpol/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
vanderpol/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

vanderpol/div.name: ∇·F
vanderpol/div.details: ∇·F = μ(1 − x²): changes sign at |x| = 1 — Bendixson's criterion allows the limit cycle only because the divergence is not of one sign.

hopf/F.name: F
hopf/F.summary: ṙ = r(μ − r²), θ̇ = ω in Cartesian form (μ = 1, ω = 3)
hopf/F.details: ṙ = r(μ − r²), θ̇ = ω in Cartesian form (μ = 1, ω = 3): the supercritical Hopf normal form past the bifurcation. The origin is an unstable spiral; the circle r = √μ is an attracting limit cycle. At μ ≤ 0 the origin would be a stable spiral and the cycle gone.

hopf/speed.name: |F|
hopf/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
hopf/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

hopf/r2dot.name: ∇r²·F
hopf/r2dot.details: ∇(r²)·F = 2r²(μ − r²): positive inside the cycle, negative outside, zero on it — the radial dynamics that trap every orbit onto r = √μ.

lotka/F.name: F
lotka/F.summary: ẋ = x(α − βy), ẏ = y(δx − γ) (all 1)
lotka/F.details: ẋ = x(α − βy), ẏ = y(δx − γ) (all 1): prey x, predators y. The coexistence point (γ/δ, α/β) = (1, 1) is a center — every orbit is a closed cycle, the amplitude set by the initial condition; the origin is a saddle (axes invariant).

lotka/C.name: C (first integral)
lotka/C.details: C = δx − γ ln x + βy − α ln y is conserved (minimum 2 at (1, 1)): its isolines are the population cycles.
lotka/C.summary: C = δx − γ ln x + βy − α ln y is conserved (minimum 2 at (1, 1))

lotka/speed.name: |F|
lotka/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
lotka/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

competition/F.name: F
competition/F.details: ẋ = x(3 − x − 2y), ẏ = y(2 − x − y): two species competing for the same resource (Strogatz §6.4). Bistable: (3, 0) and (0, 2) are stable nodes, (1, 1) a saddle whose stable manifold (drawn) separates the basins — one species always excludes the other; the origin is an unstable node.

competition/speed.name: |F|
competition/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
competition/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

competition/div.name: ∇·F
competition/div.details: Divergence of the flow: negative where phase volume contracts, positive where it expands.

saddlefocus/F.name: F
saddlefocus/F.details: ẋ = −0.2x − y, ẏ = x − 0.2y, ż = 0.4z: eigenvalues −0.2 ± i and +0.4. Orbits spiral in towards the z axis while being pushed away from the xy plane: a saddle-focus, the local picture at the Lorenz and Rössler equilibria (with the roles of the spiral and the axis swapped for Rössler).

saddlefocus/inv.name: z²·r⁴ (invariant)
saddlefocus/inv.details: d ln(r²)/dt = −0.4 and d ln(z²)/dt = 0.8, so z²(x² + y²)² is conserved: every orbit stays on one of its level surfaces (hourglasses pinched at the plane and the axis).
saddlefocus/inv.summary: d ln(r²)/dt = −0.4 and d ln(z²)/dt = 0.8, so z²(x² + y²)² is conserved

saddlefocus/speed.name: |F|
saddlefocus/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
saddlefocus/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

gradient3/F.name: F
gradient3/F.details: F = −∇V, V = ¼Σ(xᵢ² − 1)²: steepest descent in a volume. 27 equilibria: 8 minima (sinks), 12 index-1 saddles, 6 index-2 saddles, 1 maximum (source); the flow is normal to the isosurfaces of V.

gradient3/V.name: V
gradient3/V.summary: V = ¼Σ(xᵢ² − 1)², the triple double well
gradient3/V.details: The triple double well; isosurfaces at low levels are 8 blobs around the minima, merging through the saddles as the level rises.

gradient3/speed.name: |F|
gradient3/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
gradient3/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

gradient3/gradV.name: ∇V
gradient3/gradV.summary: the exact gradient of the potential; F = −∇V

lorenz/F.name: F
lorenz/F.summary: ẋ = σ(y − x), ẏ = x(ρ − z) − y, ż = xy − βz with σ = 10, ρ = 28, β = 8/3
lorenz/F.details: ẋ = σ(y − x), ẏ = x(ρ − z) − y, ż = xy − βz with σ = 10, ρ = 28, β = 8/3. The origin is a saddle (1 unstable, 2 stable directions); C± = (±√(β(ρ−1)), ±√(β(ρ−1)), ρ − 1) are saddle-foci (a 2D unstable spiral, 1 stable direction). ∇·F = −(σ + 1 + β) = −13.67: phase volume shrinks, so the attractor (drawn) has zero volume.

lorenz/speed.name: |F|
lorenz/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
lorenz/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

lorenz/trap.name: V (trapping)
lorenz/trap.details: V = ρx² + σy² + σ(z − 2ρ)²: a Lyapunov-like function whose derivative is negative outside a bounded ellipsoid (see V̇), so every orbit enters and stays in a trapping region. Isosurfaces are ellipsoids centred on (0, 0, 2ρ).

lorenz/trapdot.name: ∇V·F
lorenz/trapdot.details: V̇ = ∇V·F = −2σ[ρx² + y² + β(z − ρ)² − βρ²] (exact symbolic derivative): positive only inside the small ellipsoid ρx² + y² + β(z − ρ)² = βρ² — the isosurface V̇ = 0 — where the attractor lives.
lorenz/trapdot.summary: V̇ = ∇V·F = −2σ[ρx² + y² + β(z − ρ)² − βρ²] (exact symbolic derivative)

rossler/F.name: F
rossler/F.details: ẋ = −y − z, ẏ = x + ay, ż = b + z(x − c), a = b = 0.2, c = 5.7. Near the plane z ≈ 0 the flow is the unstable spiral ẋ = −y, ẏ = x + ay; the ż equation folds the spiral's outer part up and back over (a Möbius-band-like attractor, drawn). Two equilibria: P₋ near the origin is a saddle-focus (spiral out in the plane, attracting along one direction), P₊ far outside the box.

rossler/speed.name: |F|
rossler/speed.summary: the speed of the flow; zero exactly at the equilibria
rossler/speed.details: |F|: the speed of the flow (log codomain). Zero exactly at the equilibria, so its low isolines / isosurfaces ring them.

rossler/div.name: ∇·F
rossler/div.details: ∇·F = a + x − c: negative over the attractor except where x > c − a = 5.5, the fold region where the flow expands.

name: dynamical systems (textbook)
summary: Textbook continuous dynamical systems ẋ = F(x), one space each: linear zoo, gradient flows, pendulum, Duffing, Van der Pol, Hopf, Lotka–Volterra, competition, saddle-focus, Lorenz, Rössler.
details:
Continuous dynamical systems ẋ = F(x), one space per system, the time evolution F as a symbolic vector field (the space's `flow`, so streamlines and glyphs follow it forward in time; turn on the S and V columns of the fields panel).

In every space: |F| is the speed (zero at the equilibria); H / V / C are energies, potentials and first integrals whose level sets are orbits or are cut orthogonally by them; ∇H·F, ∇V·F, ∇r²·F are exact symbolic Lyapunov derivatives; ∇·F the divergence. Equilibria are labelled by type; limit cycles, strange attractors and separatrices are ordered point sets integrated by RK4 from the same expression trees. Parameters (γ, δ, μ, σ ρ β, …) are `consts` of each F and can be edited in the JSON.

Each space's ⓘ says what it shows. Generated by tools/dynamical-systems/build.mjs.
